description.en: Given the head of a singly linked list, print all elements from head to tail separated by spaces.
description.hi: Singly linked list ka head diya gaya hai. Head se tail tak saare elements space se separated print karo.

explanation.en: Traverse from head to tail and print each node's value.
explanation.hi: Head se tail tak traverse karo aur har node ki value print karo.

hints.en: Use a while loop with a current pointer starting at head.
hints.hi: Head se shuru karke ek current pointer ke saath while loop use karo.

starterCode.javascript: function printList(head) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: Traverse the linked list starting from head. At each node, print the data. Move to next node until NULL.
approach.hi: Head se linked list traverse karo. Har node par data print karo. NULL milne tak next node par jao.

code.python:
def print_list(head):
    curr = head
    parts = []
    while curr:
        parts.append(str(curr.data))
        curr = curr.next
    print(' '.join(parts))

description.en: Given the head of a linked list and a value, insert a new node with that value at the beginning. Return the new head.
description.hi: Linked list ka head aur ek value di gayi hai. Us value ka naya node beginning mein insert karo. Naya head return karo.

explanation.en: New node with value 1 is added at the beginning.
explanation.hi: Value 1 wala naya node beginning mein add kiya gaya.

hints.en: Create new node, set its next to current head, return new node as new head.
hints.hi: Naya node banao, uska next current head pe set karo, naya node return karo.

starterCode.javascript: function insertAtBeginning(head, val) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: Create a new node with the given value, set its next pointer to the current head, and return the new node as the new head. This is O(1).
approach.hi: Di gayi value ka naya node banao, uska next pointer current head pe set karo, aur naya node naya head banake return karo. Yeh O(1) hai.

code.python: def insert_at_beginning(head, val):\n    n = Node(val); n.next = head; return n
code.java: public Node insertAtBeginning(Node head, int val) {\n    Node n = new Node(val); n.next = head; return n;\n}
code.javascript: function insertAtBeginning(head, val) {\n    const n = { data: val, next: head }; return n;\n}
code.c: Node* insertAtBeginning(Node* head, int val) {\n    Node* n = malloc(sizeof(Node)); n->data=val; n->next=head; return n;\n}

description.en: Given the head of a linked list and a value, insert a new node with that value at the end. Return the head.
description.hi: Linked list ka head aur ek value di gayi hai. Us value ka naya node end mein insert karo. Head return karo.

explanation.en: New node with value 4 appended at end.
explanation.hi: Value 4 wala node end mein add kiya gaya.

hints.en: Traverse to the last node and set its next to the new node.
hints.hi: Last node tak traverse karo aur uska next naye node pe set karo.

starterCode.javascript: function insertAtEnd(head, val) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: If list is empty, return new node as head. Otherwise traverse to last node (where next is NULL) and attach the new node.
approach.hi: Agar list empty hai toh naya node head ke roop mein return karo. Warna last node tak traverse karo (jahan next NULL ho) aur naya node attach karo.

code.python:
def insert_at_end(head, val):
    n = Node(val)
    if not head: return n
    curr = head
    while curr.next: curr = curr.next
    curr.next = n
    return head

description.en: Given the head of a linked list and a key, delete the first occurrence of the node with that key value. Return the new head.
description.hi: Linked list ka head aur ek key di gayi hai. Us key value wale node ki pehli occurrence delete karo. Naya head return karo.

explanation.hi: Value 3 wala node delete ho gaya.

hints.en: Handle deletion of head separately. For other nodes, find the previous node and update its next.
hints.hi: Head deletion alag handle karo. Baaki nodes ke liye previous node dhundho aur uska next update karo.

starterCode.javascript: function deleteNode(head, key) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: If head is the target, return head.next. Otherwise traverse to find the node before the target and update its next pointer to skip the target node.
approach.hi: Agar head target hai toh head.next return karo. Warna target se pehle wale node tak traverse karo aur uska next pointer update karke target skip karo.

code.python:
def delete_node(head, key):
    if not head: return None
    if head.data == key: return head.next
    curr = head
    while curr.next and curr.next.data != key: curr = curr.next
    if curr.next: curr.next = curr.next.next
    return head

description.en: Given the head of a linked list, find and return its length (number of nodes).
description.hi: Linked list ka head diya gaya hai. Iska length (nodes ki sankhya) dhundho aur return karo.

hints.en: Use a counter and traverse the entire list.
hints.hi: Counter use karo aur poori list traverse karo.

starterCode.javascript: function findLength(head) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: Initialize count to 0. Traverse the list incrementing count at each node. Return count.
approach.hi: Count ko 0 se initialize karo. List traverse karo aur har node par count increment karo. Count return karo.

code.python:
def find_length(head):
    count = 0
    while head: count += 1; head = head.next
    return count

description.en: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the reversed list's head.
description.hi: Singly linked list ka head diya gaya hai. List reverse karo aur reversed list ka head return karo.

explanation.hi: List 1->2->3->4->5 reverse hokar 5->4->3->2->1 ban jaati hai.

hints.en: Use three pointers: prev (starts null), curr (starts at head), next. At each step, reverse the link.
hints.hi: Teen pointers use karo: prev (null se shuru), curr (head se shuru), next. Har step par link reverse karo.

starterCode.javascript: function reverseList(head) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: Iterative approach: use three pointers prev=NULL, curr=head, next. For each node, save next, point curr.next to prev, move prev to curr, move curr to saved next. Return prev as new head.
approach.hi: Iterative approach: teen pointers use karo prev=NULL, curr=head, next. Har node ke liye, next save karo, curr.next ko prev pe point karo, prev ko curr pe move karo, curr ko saved next pe move karo. prev ko naya head banake return karo.

code.python:
def reverse_list(head):
    prev, curr = None, head
    while curr:
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
    return prev

description.en: Given the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle (a node that is revisited during traversal). Return true if cycle exists, false otherwise.
description.hi: Linked list ka head diya gaya hai. Check karo ki list mein cycle hai ya nahi (koi node traverse ke dauran dobara visit ho). True return karo agar cycle hai, warna false.

examples.input: head = [3, 2, 0, -4], pos = 1 (tail connects to node at index 1)

explanation.en: There is a cycle: tail connects back to node with value 2.
explanation.hi: Cycle hai: tail node wapas value 2 wale node se connect hai.

hints.en: Use Floyd's cycle detection: slow pointer moves 1 step, fast pointer moves 2 steps.
hints.hi: Floyd's cycle detection use karo: slow pointer 1 step, fast pointer 2 steps move karta hai.

starterCode.javascript: function hasCycle(head) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm: move slow by 1 and fast by 2. If they meet, there's a cycle. If fast reaches NULL, no cycle.
approach.hi: Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm: slow 1 se aur fast 2 se move karo. Agar mile toh cycle hai. Fast NULL tak pahunche toh cycle nahi hai.

code.python:
def has_cycle(head):
    slow = fast = head
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
        if slow is fast: return True
    return False

For even length, return second middle node (4).

description.en: Given the heads of two sorted linked lists, merge them into one sorted linked list and return its head.
description.hi: Do sorted linked lists ke heads diye gaye hain. Inhe ek sorted linked list mein merge karo aur head return karo.

explanation.en: Merge two sorted lists by comparing nodes one by one.
explanation.hi: Dono sorted lists ko ek-ek node compare karke merge karo.

hints.en: Use a dummy head node. Compare nodes from both lists and link the smaller one to the result.
hints.hi: Dummy head node use karo. Dono lists ke nodes compare karo aur chhote wale ko result se link karo.

starterCode.javascript: function mergeTwoLists(l1, l2) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: Use a dummy node as the head of the result. Compare l1 and l2 node values; attach the smaller one to result. Move the pointer of the list whose node was attached. Attach remaining nodes at end.
approach.hi: Dummy node result ka head banao. l1 aur l2 node values compare karo; chhote wale ko result se attach karo. Jis list ka node attach hua uska pointer move karo. Baaki nodes end mein attach karo.

code.python:
def merge_two_lists(l1, l2):
    dummy = Node(0); curr = dummy
    while l1 and l2:
        if l1.data <= l2.data: curr.next=l1; l1=l1.next
        else: curr.next=l2; l2=l2.next
        curr = curr.next
    curr.next = l1 or l2
    return dummy.next

problems.title: Remove Nth Node from End
problems.titleHi: End se Nth Node Remove Karo

description.en: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end of the list and return its head.
description.hi: Linked list ka head diya gaya hai. List ke end se nth node remove karo aur head return karo.

explanation.en: The 2nd node from end (value 4) is removed.
explanation.hi: End se 2nd node (value 4) remove ho gayi.

hints.en: Use two pointers with n-step gap. When fast reaches end, slow is at the node before the target.
hints.hi: N-step gap wale do pointers use karo. Fast end par pahunche tab slow target se pehle wale node par hoga.

starterCode.javascript: function removeNthFromEnd(head, n) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: Use a dummy node before head. Move fast pointer n+1 steps ahead, then move both slow and fast together until fast is null. Remove the node after slow.
approach.hi: Head se pehle dummy node use karo. Fast pointer ko n+1 steps aage le jao, phir slow aur fast dono ko saath move karo jab tak fast null ho. Slow ke baad wala node remove karo.

code.python:
def remove_nth_from_end(head, n):
    dummy = Node(0); dummy.next = head
    slow = fast = dummy
    for _ in range(n + 1): fast = fast.next
    while fast: slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next
    slow.next = slow.next.next
    return dummy.next

problems.title: Intersection of Two Linked Lists

description.en: Given the heads of two singly linked lists, find the node at which they intersect. Return null if no intersection.
description.hi: Do singly linked lists ke heads diye gaye hain. Woh node dhundho jahan dono intersect karte hain. Agar koi intersection nahi hai toh null return karo.

examples.input: listA = [4,1,8,4,5], listB = [5,6,1,8,4,5] (intersect at node with value 8)

explanation.en: Both lists share nodes starting from node with value 8.
explanation.hi: Dono lists value 8 wale node se nodes share karti hain.

constraints: Intersection is by reference, not value

hints.en: Use two pointers starting at headA and headB. When one reaches null, redirect it to the other list's head.
hints.hi: headA aur headB se do pointers start karo. Jab ek null reach kare toh use doosri list ke head par redirect karo.

starterCode.javascript: function getIntersectionNode(headA, headB) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: Use two pointers pA and pB. Traverse both. When pA reaches end, redirect to headB. When pB reaches end, redirect to headA. They will meet at intersection (or both null if no intersection) after at most m+n steps.
approach.hi: Do pointers pA aur pB use karo. Dono traverse karo. pA end reach kare toh headB pe redirect karo. pB end reach kare toh headA pe redirect karo. Woh intersection par milenge (ya dono null agar intersection nahi) m+n steps mein.

description.en: A doubly linked list where some nodes have a child pointer to another doubly linked list. Flatten the list so all nodes appear in a single-level doubly linked list. The child list should be inserted after the node and before the node's next.
description.hi: Ek doubly linked list hai jahan kuch nodes mein ek child pointer hota hai jo doosri doubly linked list ko point karta hai. List ko flatten karo taaki saare nodes single-level doubly linked list mein aayein. Child list node ke baad aur node ke next se pehle insert honi chahiye.

examples.input: 1 - 2 - 3 - 4 - 5 - 6 with 3 having child 7 - 8 - 9 - 10 with 8 having child 11 - 12

explanation.en: The child list of 3 is inserted after 3. The child list of 8 is inserted after 8.
explanation.hi: 3 ki child list 3 ke baad insert hoti hai. 8 ki child list 8 ke baad insert hoti hai.

hints.en: Use a stack or recursion. At each node with a child, insert the child list between current and next.
hints.hi: Stack ya recursion use karo. Child wale har node par, child list ko current aur next ke beech insert karo.

starterCode.javascript: function flatten(head) {\n    // Write your code here\n}

approach.en: Iterate through the list. When a node with a child is found, find the tail of the child list, connect it to the current node's next, then insert the child list between current and current's original next. Set child to null.
approach.hi: List iterate karo. Child wala node milne par, child list ki tail dhundho, use current node ke next se connect karo, phir child list ko current aur original next ke beech insert karo. Child null set karo.

code.python:
def flatten(head):
    curr = head
    while curr:
        if curr.child:
            child = curr.child
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = child
            child.prev = curr
            curr.child = None
            tail = child
            while tail.next: tail = tail.next
            tail.next = nxt
            if nxt: nxt.prev = tail
        curr = curr.next
    return head
